summary: px8my ships a browser redirect payload distributed via jsDelivr CDN
details: The package's main file `px.js` is browser-only code that injects a full-viewport iframe pointing at `https://mfmz.tngmex.cn/H.html?c=0gjr`. A shipped helper script `update_px8my.sh` documents a workflow to rotate the destination domain, bump the version, run `npm publish`, and purge the jsDelivr cache at `purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js` — indicating the package exists to serve mutable redirect JavaScript to third-party websites via the `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js` URL, not to be consumed by Node installers. There are no lifecycle scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall), and `require`-ing the package in Node would throw on the undefined `document` global. Installing this package into a Node project has no install-time or import-time effect on the installer. The harm is directed at end users of external websites that embed the jsDelivr URL, who get redirected to the attacker-controlled domain — a CDN-abuse / malvertising delivery mechanism, not a supply-chain attack against npm installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
